script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 2. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Every living system produces waste—byproducts, toxins, things that don't serve anymore.  Without elimination, waste accumulates and poisons.  Excretion isn't glamorous, but it's essential.

Excretion isn't passive—it requires energy and systems. Kidneys actively filter blood. Liver processes toxins. Lungs expel CO2. Waste removal is active work, not automatic disappearance. When excretion fails, toxins build up.  Kidney failure means waste in blood.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Outputs include waste.  Systems that can't eliminate what they don't need become toxic.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Elimination Practice - What Needs to Go?.

Here's your activity: What's accumulated in your life that no longer serves? Commitments, possessions, habits, relationships? Pick one thing to eliminate this week. Regular clearing prevents toxic buildup. Excretion is essential. This helps you identify and remove accumulated waste.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about getting rid of waste can be applied to elimination practice - what needs to go?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
